specimen_type: Stomach, laparoscopic wedge resection of a gastric wall mass

sections.Clinical details: 54-year-old woman with a submucosal mass of the gastric body. Laparoscopic wedge resection performed.
sections.Specimen: Stomach, laparoscopic wedge resection of gastric wall mass. Received fresh, fixed in formalin.
sections.Gross description: Wedge of gastric wall measuring 80 x 60 x 25 mm. Serosal surface smooth and intact. Within the wall is a well-circumscribed, lobulated, grey-white submucosal mass measuring 55 mm in greatest dimension. Cut surface is fleshy and whorled with focal haemorrhage. Overlying mucosa is intact. All margins are clear, the closest being 8 mm from the tumour. Sections taken from the tumour, the closest margin and the serosal surface.
sections.Microscopic description: Tumour composed of intersecting fascicles of spindle cells with moderate cellularity, elongated nuclei and mild to moderate nuclear atypia. Mitotic figures number 3 per 5 mm2. No tumour necrosis identified. Serosa is intact and not involved. Closest resection margin is free of tumour, 8 mm from the tumour edge. Lymphovascular and perineural invasion not identified.
sections.Immunohistochemistry: Tumour cells show diffuse strong positivity for CD117 and DOG1 and are positive for CD34. Desmin, S100 and smooth muscle actin are negative.
sections.Diagnosis:
Stomach, gastric body, laparoscopic wedge resection:
Gastrointestinal stromal tumour (GIST), spindle cell type, 55 mm, mitotic count 3 per 5 mm2.
Resection margins free of tumour; closest margin 8 mm.
Lymphovascular and perineural invasion not identified.
No lymph nodes submitted.
pT3 (AJCC 8th edition).
sections.Synoptic summary:
Tumour size: 55 mm
Histologic grade: Not applicable
Margins: Free; closest 8 mm
Lymphovascular invasion: Not identified
Perineural invasion: Not identified
Lymph nodes (positive/total): Not applicable (none submitted)
pT: pT3
pN: Not applicable
Staging edition: AJCC 8th edition
sections.Comment: In AJCC 8th edition staging of gastric GIST, the T category is assigned by tumour size. A tumour greater than 5 cm and up to 10 cm is pT3 irrespective of serosal status, and the serosa is intact here. Using Miettinen criteria, a gastric tumour of 5.1 to 10 cm with 5 or fewer mitoses per 50 high-power fields (equivalent to 5 mm2) is classified as intermediate risk. Multidisciplinary discussion is advised regarding adjuvant therapy.
